Slavery is an interesting institution. You see the same things repeating in the US that you did in Ancient Rome. Owners would want to manumit their slaves upon their deaths (but not before). The decedent’s inheritors would want to prevent the manumission to the extent possible. The authorities who also owned slaves and weren’t dying didn’t like the practice because of its effect on their slaves. So they would pass laws limiting manumission. Eventually the system falls apart on its own, but it can take centuries and then is replaced by a similar system relatively quickly.

The period from the mid-18th century Enlightenment to now is really notable for how much freer the vast majority of people have become even as countervailing forces work to rein it back. Things are starting to look darker, though, I fear.
